# Copilot instructions

- Treat the wiki as the source of truth for research knowledge. Keep one canonical Markdown page per paper or article, with metadata and typed links in frontmatter. Derive indexes and graphs from the wiki rather than maintaining a separate knowledge store.
- Ground claims in sources; popularity is not evidence. Use deterministic code for schema validation, ID resolution, and deduplication.
- When recommending papers, consider the reader's interests and what each paper adds to the existing wiki, not just citations, awards, or popularity. Honor explicit ranking or sampling requests, and do not assume the reader has read every wiki entry.
- When a reading search surfaces a paper with verified Best Paper, Outstanding Paper, Spotlight, or Oral recognition or presentation, add it to [the conference paper catalog](../discovery/resources/bestpaper_list.md#verified-papers). Record the paper link, venue, year, exact label, and official evidence URL. Add newly verified labels to existing entries instead of duplicating papers. Do not infer labels or treat a presentation as an award.
- Keep schemas, workflow skills, task prompts, and harness orchestration separate.
- For paper questions, check the wiki and matching local extract in `sources/` before re-fetching; consult the original when the extract is insufficient. Append a concise, sourced H3 Q&A to the **FAQ** unless already covered. Leave the rest of the page unchanged and validate.
- Apply and verify accepted paper-specific corrections in the canonical wiki page. When human feedback identifies a concrete wiki or workflow improvement, save a concise, non-sensitive summary under `feedback/`. Link the affected page or workflow, state the expected improvement, and update an existing record rather than duplicating it. Link a relevant GitHub issue or pull request when one exists. Consult retained feedback when reviewing recurring workflow gaps; do not turn one-off paper corrections into general rules. Do not save raw comments or evaluation notes in feedback records, wiki pages, or skill files.
